assessments.reasoning: RsyncProject/rsync publishes COPYING at commit 02cfb7621cfea47b49aa30886ab0e4e3e03e78f8. All three contiguous parts cover the 35,566-byte file and report the claim’s revision digest. The controlling passage is the opening “REGARDING OPENSSL AND XXHASH” paragraph.

The License Index’s own SCOPE.md at cdff8aeed68bf1f9c62d8c86159c7dc08b2d75d7, bytes [640,783), admits an additional permission or documented modification. The rsync holders’ express permission satisfies the first branch. The rule reserves affected editions for separate support.

challenge.method: Under SCES-1.0 §§1, 3–4 and Codex Research Protocol stage 7, I tested whether the opening paragraph merely comments on GPL System Libraries or grants a separate permission. I compared its operative language with GPL §§1, 6 and 7 and the closing sample notice. The policy pin is ab26f278422772f2d9e5d4dd016407d14372a710, adopted bundle SHA-256 14da3f31f697ab828d4a4560f060dbe511861020db54bea7bc531e20ea0855ce.
challenge.results: The holders expressly “give permission” before stating that the combination is “also considered” covered by System Libraries. The second sentence records the project’s interpretation. The first independently establishes the documentary exception, with its linkage and distribution limits intact.

limitations: The grant identifies rsync, the two libraries, dynamic linkage and the libraries’ distribution terms. Other linkage modes and revisions require separate evidence.

COPYING reproduces GPL version 3. Its sample application notice does not establish a version election for any particular rsync file. The broader legal interpretation of System Libraries is also outside this identity finding.
reasoning: The opening paragraph of the pinned rsync COPYING expressly grants permission to link rsync dynamically with OpenSSL and xxHash and to distribute the dynamically linked combination when the libraries are distributed in compliance with their licenses. That grant meets the Index criterion for a license exception. “rsync Linking Exception” and “active” are editorial values for this reference.
